Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$\gamma>0$, $H_0=-\Delta$ on $L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ and
$H_\gamma:=-\Delta-\gamma/|\cdot|$ on $D(H_\gamma)=H^2(\mathbb R^3)$, the
self-adjoint Coulomb operator established below on this exact domain, with
essential spectrum $[0,\infty)$ as proved by the local compact-resolvent argument. Use the physical-momentum Fourier transform $\mathcal F_pf(p)=(2\pi)^{-3/2}\mathcal F_2f(p/(2\pi))$, unitary by the dilation change of variables, equivalently $(2\pi)^{-3/2}\int e^{-ip\cdot x}f(x)dx$ on Schwartz functions. Let $P_j=\mathcal F_p^*M_{p_j}\mathcal F_p=-i\partial_j$ on its maximal weak-derivative domain; thus $H_0=\mathcal F_p^*M_{|p|^2}\mathcal F_p$. Set $a(p)=\gamma/(2|p|)$ for $p\ne0$ and $a(0)=0$, and $a(P)=\mathcal F_p^*M_a\mathcal F_p$ on the maximal multiplier domain. For $|t|\ge1$ define the
Dollard-modified free evolution
$$U_D(t):=e^{-itH_0}e^{i\,\operatorname{sign}(t)\,a(P)\log|t|}$$
(the two factors commute, being functions of $P$; extend to $|t|\le1$ by
$U_D(t):=e^{-itH_0}$). Then:

(a) $U_D(t)$ is unitary for every $t$ and strongly continuous in $t$ away from $t=0$; on the dense set of momentum $C_c^\infty$ vectors supported in an annulus $0<a_0\le|p|\le b_0<\infty$ it is differentiable for $|t|>1$, with the exterior one-sided derivatives at $t=\pm1$, and
$$i\,U_D'(t)=\Bigl[H_0-\frac{\gamma}{2|t|\,|P|}\Bigr]U_D(t)\qquad(|t|>1).$$

(b) *Integrable remainder.* For every vector $\psi$ in that dense set one has
$$\int_1^\infty\Bigl\|\Bigl[\frac{\gamma}{|\cdot|}-\frac{\gamma}{2|t|\,|P|}\Bigr]U_D(t)\psi\Bigr\|_2dt<\infty,$$
and the same integral with $|t|$ in the comparison denominator over $(-\infty,-1]$ is finite. More precisely, for each such $\psi$ there are $T_\psi\ge1$ and $C_\psi<\infty$ such that for both signs of $t$, $|t|\ge T_\psi$ implies $\|[\gamma/|\cdot|-\gamma/(2|t|\,|P|)]U_D(t)\psi\|_2\le C_\psi(1+\log|t|)/|t|^2$.

No empirical claim, no Rutherford cross-section and no photon interpretation is
asserted; the logarithmic phase is a comparison construction for the
long-range generator.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\gamma>0$,
$H_0=-\Delta$, $H_\gamma=-\Delta-\gamma/|\cdot|$ on $H^2(\mathbb R^3)$, and let
$U_D(t)$ be the Dollard-modified evolution of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-dollard-integrable-remainder]], with modified wave operators $\Omega_{D\pm}=\operatorname{s-lim}_{t\to\pm\infty}e^{itH_\gamma}U_D(t)$, whose existence on all of $L^2$ is included in the claimed conclusion. Then:

(a) $\Omega_{D\pm}e^{-isH_0}=e^{-isH_\gamma}\Omega_{D\pm}$ for all $s$;

(b) *Per-channel form.* With the Coulomb angular-radial unitary
$\widehat T_{\gamma,l}$ and its free analogue $\widehat T_{0,l}$ constructed
below with regular coefficient one and density $\sqrt E/(\pi|W_l(\sqrt E)|^2)$, the operator $\Omega_{D\pm}$ acts in
each angular channel as multiplication by a bounded Borel function $b_{l,\pm}(E)$
of the energy;

(c) *Completeness.* $|b_{l,\pm}(E)|=1$ for a.e. $E>0$, hence
$\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{D\pm}=H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H_\gamma)=H_{\mathrm{c}}(H_\gamma)$
and the modified scattering operator $S_D=\Omega_{D+}^*\Omega_{D-}$ is unitary
on $L^2(\mathbb R^3)$.

The statement covers the exactly Coulombic two-body model with $\gamma>0$; it
does not assert explicit scattering amplitudes or measured cross sections.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $T$ be a self-adjoint operator on the nonzero
complex Hilbert space $H$. Then there is a unique regular projection valued
measure $E$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ such that
$$
D(T)=\Bigl\{x\in H:\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^2\,dE_x(\lambda)<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad Tx=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,dE(\lambda)x\quad(x\in D(T)).
$$
Conversely, if $E$ is a regular projection valued measure on $\mathbb R$, then
the operator $\int\lambda\,dE$ with that domain is self-adjoint and its
spectral projection valued measure is $E$ again.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $(X,\Sigma)$ be a measurable space, let $H$ be a
nonzero complex Hilbert space, let $E$ be a projection valued measure on
$(X,\Sigma)$, and let $f:X\to\mathbb C$ be bounded and $\Sigma$-measurable
([[def-measurable-function-between-measurable-spaces]]). Then:

1. there is a unique operator $\Phi_E(f)\in\mathcal B(H)$ with
   $$\langle\Phi_E(f)x,y\rangle=\int f\,dE_{x,y}\qquad(x,y\in H),$$
   and for every sequence $(s_n)$ of complex simple functions with
   $\|f-s_n\|_\infty\to0$ one has $\|\Phi_E(f)-\int s_n\,dE\|\to0$: the integral
   is obtained from uniform simple approximations and is independent of the
   approximating sequence;
2. $\|\Phi_E(f)\|\le\|f\|_\infty$, and for every $x\in H$
$$\langle\Phi_E(f)x,x\rangle=\int f\,dE_x,\qquad \|\Phi_E(f)x\|^2=\int|f|^2\,dE_x ;$$
3. the exact norm is the **$E$-essential supremum**
$$\|f\|_{E,\infty}:=\sup\bigl\{\|f\|_{\infty,E_x}:\ x\in H,\ \|x\|=1\bigr\}, \qquad \|\Phi_E(f)\|=\|f\|_{E,\infty},$$
   where $\|f\|_{\infty,E_x}$ denotes the essential supremum of the real measurable function $|f|$ with respect to
   the finite measure $E_x$ ([[def-essential-supremum-with-respect-to-a-measure]]).

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $T$ be a self-adjoint operator with spectral
projection valued measure $E$ on $\mathbb R$ acting on a complex Hilbert space $H$
([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]) and let
$f,g:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$ be Borel. Write $u(T)=u(E)$, with the truncation definition below. If $H=\{0\}$, use its unique PVM and unique full-domain operator directly. Then:

1. $f(T)^*=\overline f(T)$;
2. $f(T)g(T)$ has domain $D(g(T))\cap D((fg)(T))$ and equals the restriction of
   $(fg)(T)$ to that domain, and its closure is $(fg)(T)$;
3. on $D(f(T))\cap D(g(T))$ the sum $f(T)+g(T)$ equals the restriction of
   $(f+g)(T)$, and the closure of $f(T)+g(T)$ is $(f+g)(T)$;
4. the spectrum of $f(T)$ is the essential range
   $\{z\in\mathbb C:E(f^{-1}(B_\varepsilon(z)))\ne0$ for every
   $\varepsilon>0\}$ of $f$ with respect to $E$;
5. if $f$ is continuous then that essential range is the closure of
   $f(\sigma(T))$, with the closure redundant when $f(\sigma(T))$ is closed.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a
complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]), let $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ be a
densely defined self-adjoint operator
([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]],
[[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]]), and let $c>0$ be
real. Write $cA$ for the operator with domain $D(cA):=D(A)$ and
$(cA)x:=c\,(Ax)$. Then:

(a) $cA$ is self-adjoint.

(b) For every $z\in\mathbb C$ one has $z\in\rho(cA)$ if and only if
$z/c\in\rho(A)$, and then
$(cA-z)^{-1}=c^{-1}(A-z/c)^{-1}$; consequently
$\rho(cA)=c\,\rho(A)$ and $\sigma(cA)=c\,\sigma(A)$.

(c) If some, hence every, resolvent of $A$ is compact
([[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]],
[[def-compact-linear-operator]]), then every resolvent of $cA$ is compact,
there is a complete orthonormal family $(e_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ of eigenvectors
of $A$, the same family consists of eigenvectors of $cA$ with eigenvalues
$c\,\mu_n$, where $\mu_n$ is the eigenvalue of $e_n$ for $A$, and
$\sigma(cA)=\{c\,\mu_n:n\in\mathbb N\}$ with no other spectral points
([[lem-nrqm-intervals-compact-resolvent-eigenbasis]] clauses (b), (c)).

(d) Eigenvectors correspond exactly: for $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ and $x\in H$,
$x\ne0$, one has $x\in D(A)$ and $Ax=\lambda x$ if and only if
$x\in D(cA)$ and $(cA)x=(c\lambda)x$; and every eigenvalue of $cA$ has the same
eigenspace as the corresponding eigenvalue of $A$.

(e) If $A\ge\gamma$ in the quadratic-form sense, meaning that
$\langle Ax,x\rangle\ge\gamma\|x\|^2$ for every $x\in D(A)$, then
$cA\ge c\gamma$ in the same sense.

Only the scaling of the given operator is asserted; no domain, spectrum or
eigenvector is claimed for any other rescaling, and no physical
interpretation is attached.

strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group; the Schroedinger equation
$i\hbar\frac{d}{dt}\psi(t)=H_{\kappa}\psi(t)$ holds in the norm-differentiable
sense exactly for initial vectors $\psi(0)\in D(H_{\kappa})$, and for other
vectors the evolution is continuous but the equation is not asserted; density
preparations evolve by $\rho(t)=U(t)\rho(0)U(t)^{*}$ with $\rho(t)$ a density
operator for every $t$;

(c) *Stationary states.* For $\psi\in H_{0}$, $\psi\ne0$, the pure preparation
$[\psi]$ is stationary, $[\psi(t)]=[\psi(0)]$ for all $t$, if and only if
$\psi$ is an eigenvector of $H_{\kappa}$; in that case, with eigenvalue $E$,
one has $\psi(t)=e^{-itE/\hbar}\psi(0)$, the energy outcome law is the point
mass $\delta_{E}$ for a normalised $\psi$, and every bounded assigned sharp
observable compatible with the energy has a time-independent outcome law in
this preparation;

(d) *Position reading.* In a unit vector $\psi$ the position outcome law is
$\mu^{G}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{B}|\psi|^{2}dx$; if $\psi$ is in addition a unit
eigenvector of $H_{\kappa}$ with eigenvalue $E$, then the position density
$|\psi|^{2}$ and the energy point mass at $E$ are readings of the same
preparation through the declared observables, with no joint-measurement claim;

(e) *Spectral support and exact values.* For every preparation $\rho$ one has
$\mu^{H_{\kappa}}_{\rho}(\sigma(H_{\kappa}))=1$, and an exact energy value
$\lambda$ has $\mu^{H_{\kappa}}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})=0$ unless $\lambda$ is an
eigenvalue, in which case the probability is the total weight of the
eigenspace; in particular no exact value in $\mathbb R\setminus\sigma(H_{\kappa})$
is admissible, and the item asserts neither that $0$ is an eigenvalue nor any
statement about eigenvalues in the positive half-line, which are excluded by
the following radial items;

(f) *Scope.* The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5 and the declared
Coulomb model and the cited mathematics. It asserts no eigenvalue list, no
degeneracy, no transition, radiation or line-intensity statement, no
identification of $\kappa$, $m$ or $\hbar$ with measured constants, and no
empirical result.

after.quote:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$\gamma>0$, $H_0=-\Delta$ on $L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ and
$H_\gamma:=-\Delta-\gamma/|\cdot|$ on $D(H_\gamma)=H^2(\mathbb R^3)$, the
self-adjoint Coulomb operator established below on this exact domain, with
essential spectrum $[0,\infty)$ as proved by the local compact-resolvent argument. Use the physical-momentum Fourier transform $\mathcal F_pf(p)=(2\pi)^{-3/2}\mathcal F_2f(p/(2\pi))$, unitary by the dilation change of variables, equivalently $(2\pi)^{-3/2}\int e^{-ip\cdot x}f(x)dx$ on Schwartz functions. Let $P_j=\mathcal F_p^*M_{p_j}\mathcal F_p=-i\partial_j$ on its maximal weak-derivative domain; thus $H_0=\mathcal F_p^*M_{|p|^2}\mathcal F_p$. Set $a(p)=\gamma/(2|p|)$ for $p\ne0$ and $a(0)=0$, and $a(P)=\mathcal F_p^*M_a\mathcal F_p$ on the maximal multiplier domain. For $|t|\ge1$ define the
Dollard-modified free evolution
$$U_D(t):=e^{-itH_0}e^{i\,\operatorname{sign}(t)\,a(P)\log|t|}$$
(the two factors commute, being functions of $P$; extend to $|t|\le1$ by
$U_D(t):=e^{-itH_0}$). Then:

(a) $U_D(t)$ is unitary for every $t$ and strongly continuous in $t$ away from $t=0$; on the dense set of momentum $C_c^\infty$ vectors supported in an annulus $0<a_0\le|p|\le b_0<\infty$ it is differentiable for $|t|>1$, with the exterior one-sided derivatives at $t=\pm1$, and
$$i\,U_D'(t)=\Bigl[H_0-\frac{\gamma}{2|t|\,|P|}\Bigr]U_D(t)\qquad(|t|>1).$$

(b) *Integrable remainder.* For every vector $\psi$ in that dense set one has
$$\int_1^\infty\Bigl\|\Bigl[\frac{\gamma}{|\cdot|}-\frac{\gamma}{2|t|\,|P|}\Bigr]U_D(t)\psi\Bigr\|_2dt<\infty,$$
and the same integral with $|t|$ in the comparison denominator over $(-\infty,-1]$ is finite. More precisely, for each such $\psi$ there are $T_\psi\ge1$ and $C_\psi<\infty$ such that for both signs of $t$, $|t|\ge T_\psi$ implies $\|[\gamma/|\cdot|-\gamma/(2|t|\,|P|)]U_D(t)\psi\|_2\le C_\psi(1+\log|t|)/|t|^2$.

No empirical claim, no Rutherford cross-section and no photon interpretation is
asserted; the logarithmic phase is a comparison construction for the
long-range generator.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\gamma>0$,
$H_0=-\Delta$, $H_\gamma=-\Delta-\gamma/|\cdot|$ on $H^2(\mathbb R^3)$, and let
$U_D(t)$ be the Dollard-modified evolution of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-dollard-integrable-remainder]], with modified wave operators $\Omega_{D\pm}=\operatorname{s-lim}_{t\to\pm\infty}e^{itH_\gamma}U_D(t)$, whose existence on all of $L^2$ is included in the claimed conclusion. Then:

(a) $\Omega_{D\pm}e^{-isH_0}=e^{-isH_\gamma}\Omega_{D\pm}$ for all $s$;

(b) *Per-channel form.* With the Coulomb angular-radial unitary
$\widehat T_{\gamma,l}$ and its free analogue $\widehat T_{0,l}$ constructed
below with regular coefficient one and density $\sqrt E/(\pi|W_l(\sqrt E)|^2)$, the operator $\Omega_{D\pm}$ acts in
each angular channel as multiplication by a bounded Borel function $b_{l,\pm}(E)$
of the energy;

(c) *Completeness.* $|b_{l,\pm}(E)|=1$ for a.e. $E>0$, hence
$\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{D\pm}=H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H_\gamma)=H_{\mathrm{c}}(H_\gamma)$
and the modified scattering operator $S_D=\Omega_{D+}^*\Omega_{D-}$ is unitary
on $L^2(\mathbb R^3)$.

The statement covers the exactly Coulombic two-body model with $\gamma>0$; it
does not assert explicit scattering amplitudes or measured cross sections.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $T$ be a self-adjoint operator on the nonzero
complex Hilbert space $H$. Then there is a unique regular projection valued
measure $E$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ such that
$$
D(T)=\Bigl\{x\in H:\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^2\,dE_x(\lambda)<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad Tx=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,dE(\lambda)x\quad(x\in D(T)).
$$
Conversely, if $E$ is a regular projection valued measure on $\mathbb R$, then
the operator $\int\lambda\,dE$ with that domain is self-adjoint and its
spectral projection valued measure is $E$ again.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $(X,\Sigma)$ be a measurable space, let $H$ be a
nonzero complex Hilbert space, let $E$ be a projection valued measure on
$(X,\Sigma)$, and let $f:X\to\mathbb C$ be bounded and $\Sigma$-measurable
([[def-measurable-function-between-measurable-spaces]]). Then:

1. there is a unique operator $\Phi_E(f)\in\mathcal B(H)$ with
   $$\langle\Phi_E(f)x,y\rangle=\int f\,dE_{x,y}\qquad(x,y\in H),$$
   and for every sequence $(s_n)$ of complex simple functions with
   $\|f-s_n\|_\infty\to0$ one has $\|\Phi_E(f)-\int s_n\,dE\|\to0$: the integral
   is obtained from uniform simple approximations and is independent of the
   approximating sequence;
2. $\|\Phi_E(f)\|\le\|f\|_\infty$, and for every $x\in H$
$$\langle\Phi_E(f)x,x\rangle=\int f\,dE_x,\qquad \|\Phi_E(f)x\|^2=\int|f|^2\,dE_x ;$$
3. the exact norm is the **$E$-essential supremum**
$$\|f\|_{E,\infty}:=\sup\bigl\{\|f\|_{\infty,E_x}:\ x\in H,\ \|x\|=1\bigr\}, \qquad \|\Phi_E(f)\|=\|f\|_{E,\infty},$$
   where $\|f\|_{\infty,E_x}$ denotes the essential supremum of the real measurable function $|f|$ with respect to
   the finite measure $E_x$ ([[def-essential-supremum-with-respect-to-a-measure]]).

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $T$ be a self-adjoint operator with spectral
projection valued measure $E$ on $\mathbb R$ acting on a complex Hilbert space $H$
([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]) and let
$f,g:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$ be Borel. Write $u(T)=u(E)$, with the truncation definition below. If $H=\{0\}$, use its unique PVM and unique full-domain operator directly. Then:

1. $f(T)^*=\overline f(T)$;
2. $f(T)g(T)$ has domain $D(g(T))\cap D((fg)(T))$ and equals the restriction of
   $(fg)(T)$ to that domain, and its closure is $(fg)(T)$;
3. on $D(f(T))\cap D(g(T))$ the sum $f(T)+g(T)$ equals the restriction of
   $(f+g)(T)$, and the closure of $f(T)+g(T)$ is $(f+g)(T)$;
4. the spectrum of $f(T)$ is the essential range
   $\{z\in\mathbb C:E(f^{-1}(B_\varepsilon(z)))\ne0$ for every
   $\varepsilon>0\}$ of $f$ with respect to $E$;
5. if $f$ is continuous then that essential range is the closure of
   $f(\sigma(T))$, with the closure redundant when $f(\sigma(T))$ is closed.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a
complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]), let $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ be a
densely defined self-adjoint operator
([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]],
[[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]]), and let $c>0$ be
real. Write $cA$ for the operator with domain $D(cA):=D(A)$ and
$(cA)x:=c\,(Ax)$. Then:

(a) $cA$ is self-adjoint.

(b) For every $z\in\mathbb C$ one has $z\in\rho(cA)$ if and only if
$z/c\in\rho(A)$, and then
$(cA-z)^{-1}=c^{-1}(A-z/c)^{-1}$; consequently
$\rho(cA)=c\,\rho(A)$ and $\sigma(cA)=c\,\sigma(A)$.

(c) If some, hence every, resolvent of $A$ is compact
([[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]],
[[def-compact-linear-operator]]), then every resolvent of $cA$ is compact,
there is a complete orthonormal family $(e_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ of eigenvectors
of $A$, the same family consists of eigenvectors of $cA$ with eigenvalues
$c\,\mu_n$, where $\mu_n$ is the eigenvalue of $e_n$ for $A$, and
$\sigma(cA)=\{c\,\mu_n:n\in\mathbb N\}$ with no other spectral points
([[lem-nrqm-intervals-compact-resolvent-eigenbasis]] clauses (b), (c)).

(d) Eigenvectors correspond exactly: for $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ and $x\in H$,
$x\ne0$, one has $x\in D(A)$ and $Ax=\lambda x$ if and only if
$x\in D(cA)$ and $(cA)x=(c\lambda)x$; and every eigenvalue of $cA$ has the same
eigenspace as the corresponding eigenvalue of $A$.

(e) If $A\ge\gamma$ in the quadratic-form sense, meaning that
$\langle Ax,x\rangle\ge\gamma\|x\|^2$ for every $x\in D(A)$, then
$cA\ge c\gamma$ in the same sense.

Only the scaling of the given operator is asserted; no domain, spectrum or
eigenvector is claimed for any other rescaling, and no physical
interpretation is attached.

one-particle reading: the declared potential is
$$V_{\kappa}(x):=-\frac{\kappa}{|x|}\qquad(x\ne0),$$

**(c) The declared Dollard-modified comparison.** Choose a reference length $\ell_\star>0$, read in metres, as a comparison convention, and put
$$t_{\star}:=\frac{2m\ell_\star^2}{\hbar}\quad(\mathrm{s}).$$
and, for $t\ne0$, let $h_{t}:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb C$ be the bounded Borel
function
$$h_{t}(x):=\exp\Bigl(i\,\operatorname{sign}(t)\, \frac{m\kappa}{\hbar\sqrt{2mx}}\,\log\frac{|t|}{t_{\star}}\Bigr)\quad(x>0), \qquad h_{t}(0):=1 .$$
The model declares the **Dollard-modified free comparison** to be the family
$$U_{D}(t):=e^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}\,h_{t}(H^{\mathrm{free}})\quad(t\ne0), \qquad U_{D}(0):=I,$$
where $h_{t}(H^{\mathrm{free}})$ is the bounded functional calculus
([[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]] clause 1) of the self-adjoint free
operator: since $h_{t}$ is unimodular, $U_{D}(t)$ is unitary for every $t$,

**modified wave operators** of the model are the strong limits
$$\Omega_{D\pm}:=\operatorname*{s-lim}_{t\to\pm\infty}e^{itH_{\kappa}/\hbar}U_{D}(t),$$
declared when both exist, and the **modified scattering operator** is
$S_{D}:=\Omega_{D+}^{*}\Omega_{D-}$ when both exist and are isometries. The
reference length and the resulting time $t_\star$ are declared conventions. More exactly, changing the reference time from $t_\star$ to $t_\star'$ multiplies $U_D(t)$ on the right, for each sign $\sigma=\operatorname{sign}t$, by the fixed free-energy unitary
$$Q_\sigma= q_\sigma(H^{\mathrm{free}}),\qquad q_\sigma(E)=\exp\Bigl(-i\sigma\frac{m\kappa}{\hbar\sqrt{2mE}}\log\frac{t_\star'}{t_\star}\Bigr)\quad(E>0),\qquad q_\sigma(0)=1.$$
It is a bounded unimodular Borel multiplier and commutes with the free flow. Hence, when the wave operators exist, $\Omega_{D\pm}'=\Omega_{D\pm}Q_\pm$ and $S_D'=Q_+^*S_DQ_-$. The completeness and isometry properties are unchanged; these are the fixed outgoing and incoming phase conventions.

**(d) Status and scope.** Clauses (b)-(c) are declarations of the pair: a
prescribed long-range potential with its assigned energy observable, and a
modified comparison construction for it. The model asserts no formula for a
Coulomb scattering amplitude, no Rutherford cross section and no measured
quantity; the modification is a comparison construction for the long-range
generator, not a new interaction or a measured force. The ordinary
short-range comparison of
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] clause (d) is not claimed
to be complete for the Coulomb model; its completeness is established only
for the modified comparison, on this page.

before.claim: Put $\tau:=\hbar t/(2m)$; then $\tau\to\pm\infty$ with $t\to\pm\infty$, $\operatorname{sign}\tau=\operatorname{sign}t$, $\log|\tau|=\log(|t|/t_{\star})$ with $t_{\star}=2m/\hbar$, and $H_{\kappa}=cC_{\gamma}$ with $C_{\gamma}=-\Delta_{w}-\gamma/|\cdot|$ by [F4]. Hence, for $x>0$, the phase function of the definition satisfies $h_{t}(cx)=e^{i\operatorname{sign}\tau\,\gamma(2\sqrt x)^{-1}\log|\tau|}$, which is the Dollard phase $e^{i\operatorname{sign}\tau\,a(p)\log|\tau|}$ evaluated at $|p|=\sqrt x$.

By [F3] the bounded functional calculus transfers functions of $H^{\mathrm{free}}=cA_{0}$ to functions of $A_{0}=-\Delta_{w}$: $f(H^{\mathrm{free}})=(f\circ c)(A_{0})$. Applying this with $f=e^{-itx/\hbar}\cdot h_{t}(x)$ and using step 1.1 and $e^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}=e^{-i\tau A_{0}}$, one obtains $e^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}h_{t}(H^{\mathrm{free}})=e^{-i\tau A_{0}}e^{i\operatorname{sign}\tau\,a(P)\log|\tau|}=U_{D}^{\mathrm{nd}}(\tau)$ for the multiplier $a(P)$ of [F1]; hence $U_{D}(t)=U_{D}^{\mathrm{nd}}(\tau)$ for every $t$ with $|\tau|>1$, and these are the times that carry the two strong limits.

By [F1] the remainder is integrable along $U_{D}^{\mathrm{nd}}$, so [F2] gives existence of the nondimensional modified wave operators as strong limits of $e^{i\tau C_{\gamma}}U_{D}^{\mathrm{nd}}(\tau)$; by [F3] $e^{i\tau C_{\gamma}}=e^{itH_{\kappa}/\hbar}$, and by step 2.1 the physical comparison coincides with the nondimensional one at large times, so the strong limits $\Omega_{D\pm}$ exist and equal those of [F2], with the intertwining of [F2]. Since both factors $e^{itH_{\kappa}/\hbar}$ and $U_{D}(t)$ are unitary for every $t$, each product $e^{itH_{\kappa}/\hbar}U_{D}(t)$ is unitary, and a strong limit of unitaries is isometric: $\|\Omega_{D\pm}\psi\|=\lim_{t\to\pm\infty}\|e^{itH_{\kappa}/\hbar}U_{D}(t)\psi\|=\|\psi\|$ for every $\psi\in H_{0}$. This is (a).

By [F2] the ranges of the nondimensional modified wave operators equal $H_{\mathrm{ac}}(C_{\gamma})=H_{\mathrm c}(C_{\gamma})$; by [F3] the spectral subspaces of $H_{\kappa}=cC_{\gamma}$ and $C_{\gamma}$ coincide, and the operators coincide by step 3.1, so $\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{D+}=\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{D-}=H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H_{\kappa})=H_{\mathrm c}(H_{\kappa})$, which is (b).

By [F2] the nondimensional modified scattering operator is unitary; since the modified wave operators coincide with the nondimensional ones by step 3.1, $S_{D}=\Omega_{D+}^{*}\Omega_{D-}$ is unitary and inherits the commutation with the free flow, which is (c).

The definition of the model declares the modified comparison and states that the ordinary short-range comparison is not claimed complete for the Coulomb potential; no step of this proof establishes the ordinary limits, so (d) records exactly what the preceding steps give. This completes the proof.

after.claim: [Numerical SI comparison with dimensionless arguments] Write the fixed SI units as $L_0=1\,\mathrm m$, $T_0=1\,\mathrm s$, $M_0=1\,\mathrm{kg}$ and $E_0=1\,\mathrm J$. Let $m_0=m/M_0$, $h_0=\hbar/(E_0T_0)$, $k_0=\kappa/(E_0L_0)$, $L=\ell_\star/L_0>0$ and $t_0=t/T_0$ be their numerical values, and put $\gamma_0=\gamma L_0=2m_0k_0/h_0^2$, $c_0=h_0^2/(2m_0)$ and $\tau=h_0t_0/(2m_0)$. These are pure real numbers, with $\tau\to\pm\infty$ as $t\to\pm\infty$. Represent the wavefunctions in the numerical SI coordinate $q=x/L_0$, with the normalized $L^2$ coordinate map $\mathcal J_0f(q)=L_0^{3/2}f(L_0q)$, the Jacobian normalization understood in the chosen length unit. Substitution in the integral proves this map unitary; weak derivative substitution gives its exact $H^2$ domain transport. The numerical energy representatives are therefore $\mathsf H_\kappa=E_0^{-1}\mathcal J_0H_\kappa\mathcal J_0^{-1}=c_0C_{\gamma_0}$ and $\mathsf H_f=E_0^{-1}\mathcal J_0H^{\mathrm{free}}\mathcal J_0^{-1}=c_0A_0$, where $A_0=-\Delta_q$ and $C_{\gamma_0}=-\Delta_q-\gamma_0/|q|$. Thus $\mathcal J_0e^{-itH_\kappa/\hbar}\mathcal J_0^{-1}=e^{-i\tau C_{\gamma_0}}$ and similarly for the free operator. The numerical reference time is $t_{\star,0}=2m_0L^2/h_0$, so $\frac{|t|}{t_\star}=\frac{|t_0|}{t_{\star,0}}=\frac{|\tau|}{L^2},\qquad \log\frac{|t|}{t_\star}=\log|\tau|-2\log L.$ Every logarithm has a dimensionless argument; no time having units of length squared is placed inside the source logarithm.

[Exact fixed energy phases] For a positive numerical energy $e=c_0\lambda$, the phase coefficient of the physical definition is $m_0k_0/(h_0\sqrt{2m_0e})=\gamma_0/(2\sqrt\lambda)$. By [F1], $a(P)=\gamma_0/(2|P|)$ for the numerical source $A_0=|P|^2$. For $\sigma\in\{+1,-1\}$ define the fixed bounded unitary $B_{\sigma,L}=b_{\sigma,L}(A_0),\qquad b_{\sigma,L}(\lambda)=\exp\Bigl(-2i\sigma\frac{\gamma_0}{2\sqrt\lambda}\log L\Bigr)\quad(\lambda>0),\qquad b_{\sigma,L}(0)=1.$ The functions are bounded unimodular Borel functions despite their oscillation near zero, so their calculus is defined on all $L^2$ and they commute with $e^{-irA_0}$ for every $r$. Spectral correspondence [F3] and step 1.1 give, for $|\tau|\ge1$ and $\sigma=\operatorname{sign}t$, $\mathcal J_0U_D(t)\mathcal J_0^{-1}=e^{-i\tau A_0}e^{i\sigma a(P)\log|\tau|}B_{\sigma,L}=U_D^{\mathrm{nd}}(\tau)B_{\sigma,L}.$ The bounded functional calculus also transports under $\mathcal J_0$: conjugating the PVM gives a regular PVM representing the numerical operator, so spectral uniqueness identifies it and simple-function approximation gives the claimed calculus transport. ## Statement

Adopt the declared single-channel resonance model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-single-channel-resonance-model]] with channel label $l$,
mass $m>0$, action constant $\hbar>0$ and parameters $E_{r}\in\mathbb R$,
$\Gamma>0$, with the phase shift read modulo $\pi$ from $S_{l}=e^{2i\delta_{l}}$
and the channel cross-section reading $\sigma_{l}(E)$ of that definition.
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then for every $E>0$:

(a) $|S_{l}(E)|=1$, so the declared channel is elastic, and the phase shift is
$$\delta_{l}(E)=-\arctan\frac{\Gamma/2}{E-E_{r}}\quad(\text{modulo }\pi);$$

(b) the phase-shift factor is Lorentzian,
$$\sin^{2}\delta_{l}(E)=\frac{(\Gamma/2)^{2}}{(E-E_{r})^{2}+(\Gamma/2)^{2}},$$
with value $1$ at $E=E_{r}$ and value $1/2$ exactly at
$E=E_{r}\pm\Gamma/2$, so that the **half-height width in energy** of the
factor is $\Gamma$;

(c) the channel cross-section reading is
$$\sigma_{l}(E)=\frac{4\pi}{k(E)^{2}}(2l+1)\frac{(\Gamma/2)^{2}}{(E-E_{r})^{2}+(\Gamma/2)^{2}}, \qquad k(E)=\frac{\sqrt{2mE}}{\hbar},$$
read in $\mathrm{m^{2}}$, with value at the resonance energy
$$\sigma_{l}(E_{r})=\frac{4\pi\hbar^{2}}{2mE_{r}}(2l+1),$$
and the pair asserts no maximum statement for $\sigma_{l}$ itself, whose
energy dependence contains the slowly varying factor $k(E)^{-2}$ in addition
to the Lorentzian.

Every display is a conditional algebraic statement about the declared model;
no potential producing $S_{l}$, no decay law, no lifetime and no measured
quantity is asserted.
statement.after:
## Statement

Adopt the declared single-channel resonance model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-single-channel-resonance-model]] with channel label $l$,
mass $m>0$, action constant $\hbar>0$ and parameters $E_{r}\in\mathbb R$,
$\Gamma>0$, with the phase shift read modulo $\pi$ from $S_{l}=e^{2i\delta_{l}}$
and the channel cross-section reading $\sigma_{l}(E)$ of that definition.
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Put $y:=\Gamma/2>0$.
For every real $E$ define the **auxiliary real-axis Lorentzian factor**
$$L(E):=\frac{y^2}{(E-E_r)^2+y^2}.$$
This is a mathematical extension of the positive-energy phase-shift factor;
physical phase shifts, $k(E)$ and cross sections remain defined only for $E>0$.
Then:

(a) for every $E>0$, $|S_l(E)|=1$ and
$$\delta_l(E)=-\operatorname{Arg}(E-E_r+iy)\quad(\mathrm{modulo}\ \pi),$$
where for $z=x+iy$ with $y>0$, $\operatorname{Arg}z$ is the unique angle
$\theta\in(0,\pi)$ with $\cos\theta=x/\sqrt{x^2+y^2}$ and
$\sin\theta=y/\sqrt{x^2+y^2}$. Equivalently, for $E\ne E_r$ one may use
$\delta_l(E)=-\arctan(y/(E-E_r))$ modulo $\pi$; if $E=E_r>0$,
$\delta_l(E)=-\pi/2$ modulo $\pi$;

(b) for every $E>0$, $\sin^2\delta_l(E)=L(E)$. On the entire real axis,
$L(E)$ has value $1$ exactly at $E=E_r$ and value $1/2$ exactly at
$E=E_r\pm\Gamma/2$. Thus the **full-real-axis half-height width** of this
factor is $\Gamma$ for every real $E_r$. A peak or half-height location is
in the physical energy range only when that location is positive; the
width statement itself concerns $L$ on $\mathbb R$;

(c) for every $E>0$, the channel cross-section reading is
$$\sigma_l(E)=\frac{4\pi}{k(E)^2}(2l+1)L(E),\qquad k(E)=\frac{\sqrt{2mE}}{\hbar},$$
read in $\mathrm{m^2}$. If $E_r>0$, its value at that physical energy is
$$\sigma_l(E_r)=\frac{4\pi\hbar^2}{2mE_r}(2l+1).$$
If $E_r\le0$, this model defines no physical cross section at $E_r$.
No maximum statement at $E_r$ is made for $\sigma_l$ itself, whose energy
dependence also contains the factor $k(E)^{-2}$; no slow-variation
assumption on that factor is required.

Every display is a conditional algebraic statement about the declared model;
no potential producing $S_{l}$, no decay law, no lifetime and no measured
quantity is asserted.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the declared single-channel resonance model with channel label $l$, parameters $E_{r}$, $\Gamma>0$, the phase-shift and cross-section readings, and the choice hypotheses.

[F1] **The declared channel factor.** For $E>0$, $S_{l}(E)=\frac{E-E_{r}-i\Gamma/2}{E-E_{r}+i\Gamma/2}$ and $S_{l}=e^{2i\delta_{l}}$ modulo $\pi$, with $\sigma_{l}(E)=\frac{4\pi}{k(E)^{2}}(2l+1)\sin^{2}\delta_{l}(E)$ and $k(E)=\hbar^{-1}\sqrt{2mE}$ ([[def-nrqm-scattering-single-channel-resonance-model]] clause (b)).

[F2] **Resonance model algebra in the cited mathematics.** For the single-channel model $S(E)=\frac{E-E_{r}-i\Gamma/2}{E-E_{r}+i\Gamma/2}$ with $\Gamma>0$, $|S(E)|=1$ for real $E$ and $\sin^{2}\delta=(\Gamma/2)^{2}/((E-E_{r})^{2}+(\Gamma/2)^{2})$, and substituting into the phase-shift series gives the corresponding single-channel cross section ([[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-partial-wave-cross-section-convergence]] clause (c)).

[F3] **The pair's channel reading.** The channel cross-section reading of the pair is the summand of the phase-shift series of the partial-wave theorem, with $l$, $\delta_{l}$ and $k$ read as in the resonance model ([[def-nrqm-scattering-partial-wave-and-phase-shift-readings]] clause (c), [[pthm-nrqm-scattering-partial-wave-cross-section]] clause (b)).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; compute $|S_{l}|$ and the phase of the declared factor, then substitute the declared function into the model's channel reading.

**Given:** the data and hypotheses of the statement and [F1]-[F3].

1.1 For any real $E$, write $x:=E-E_r$ and $y:=\Gamma/2>0$. Then $x+iy\ne0$ and the purely algebraic ratio $R(E):=(x-iy)/(x+iy)$ has modulus one because its numerator is the conjugate of its denominator. On the physical range $E>0$, [F1] identifies $R(E)=S_l(E)$, proving the first part of (a). Defining $R$ as an auxiliary real-axis rational formula does not assign $k$ or a physical cross section outside the range $E>0$. [F1, given, algebra]

2.1 With $r:=\sqrt{x^2+y^2}>0$ and $\theta:=\operatorname{Arg}(x+iy)\in(0,\pi)$, one has $x+iy=r e^{i\theta}$ and $x-iy=r e^{-i\theta}$, hence $R(E)=e^{-2i\theta}$. For $E>0$ the phase $\delta_l=-\theta$ modulo $\pi$ therefore matches [F1]. When $x\ne0$, $\tan\theta=y/x$ and the principal arctangent gives the same angle modulo $\pi$; when $x=0$, $\theta=\pi/2$, so the phase is $-\pi/2$ with no division by zero. This proves all of (a). [F1, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 For $E>0$, $\sin^2\delta_l=\sin^2\theta=y^2/(x^2+y^2)=L(E)$, in agreement with [F2]. Independently, the real-axis formula has positive denominator for every real $E$ and satisfies $0<L(E)\le1$, with equality $L(E)=1$ exactly when $x=0$. Also $L(E)=1/2$ if and only if $x^2=y^2$, so its two real half-height points are $E_r-y$ and $E_r+y$, separated by $2y=\Gamma$. Restricting a point to the physical range requires that point to be positive; the mathematical peak and width identities impose no condition such as $E_r>y$. This proves (b). [F2, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 For $E>0$, substituting step 3.1 into [F1], [F3] gives $\sigma_l(E)=4\pi(2l+1)L(E)/k(E)^2$. If $E_r>0$, this formula is defined at $E=E_r$, where $L(E_r)=1$ and $k(E_r)^2=2mE_r/\hbar^2$, yielding the displayed resonance-centre value. If $E_r\le0$, no such physical evaluation is in the model's domain and the auxiliary $L(E_r)=1$ does not create one. The extra factor $k(E)^{-2}$ remains energy dependent, so no location-of-maximum or slow-variation assertion is used. This proves (c), retaining every real $E_r$ and positive $\Gamma$. [F1, F3, step 3.1, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- **Why no peak claim.** The auxiliary real-axis Lorentzian factor peaks at $E_r$; that peak is physical only if $E_r>0$. The full
  channel reading carries the factor $k(E)^{-2}$ as well; the pair states the
  full-real-axis half-height width of the Lorentzian factor, which is exactly $\Gamma$,
  without asserting where the maximum of $\sigma_{l}$ lies.
- **Modulo $\pi$.** Both $\sin^{2}$ and the cross-section reading are
  insensitive to the modulo-$\pi$ ambiguity of $\delta_{l}$.

**(a) Framework data.** Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero and action constant $\hbar>0$, and its partial-wave and phase-shift
reading [[def-nrqm-scattering-partial-wave-and-phase-shift-readings]] for a
declared central short-range potential. Fix a **channel label** $l\in\{0,1,2,\dots\}$
in the sense of clause (b) of that reading. Units are those of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]].

**(b) The declared single-channel resonance model.** As an additional model
assumption of the pair, fix real **resonance parameters** $E_{r}$ and
$\Gamma>0$, both read in joules, and **declare** the channel factor of the
label $l$ to be
$$S_{l}(E):=\frac{E-E_{r}-i\Gamma/2}{E-E_{r}+i\Gamma/2}\qquad(E>0),$$
read for positive energies only, with the **phase shift** of the channel read
from the relation $S_{l}=e^{2i\delta_{l}}$ modulo $\pi$ and the **channel
cross-section reading**
$$\sigma_{l}(E):=\frac{4\pi}{k(E)^{2}}(2l+1)\sin^{2}\delta_{l}(E), \qquad k(E):=\frac{\sqrt{2mE}}{\hbar},$$
read in $\mathrm{m^{2}}$. The model calls $E_{r}$ the **resonance energy** and
$\Gamma$ the **width parameter**; both are declared model parameters and
neither is identified with a measured quantity.

**(c) Status and scope.** Clauses (a)-(b) declare a conditional one-channel
model. The pair asserts no analytic continuation, no pole of the resolvent and
no property of any potential that would produce the declared factor
$S_{l}$; the model is used only to compute the induced phase shift and channel
cross section of the declared factor. In particular, no exponential decay law,
no lifetime $\hbar/\Gamma$ and no Lorentzian line shape of a measured
distribution is asserted or derived; those would be separate models with their
own assumptions and their own uncertainty qualifications.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$V\in L^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R)$ be real, bounded, central (invariant under
rotations) and supported in $B_R$, let $k>0$, and let $f_k\in C^\infty(S^2)$ be
the scattering amplitude of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-stationary-outgoing-integral-and-flux]].
Then:

(a) $f_k$ depends only on $\cos\theta=\Omega\cdot d$, and its Legendre expansion
$$f_k(\theta)=\frac1{2ik}\sum_{l\ge0}(2l+1)\bigl(S_l(k)-1\bigr)P_l(\cos\theta)$$
converges in $L^2(S^2)$ (and absolutely, since $f_k$ is smooth), where
$S_l(k)$ is a unit-modulus number determined by the regular radial solution
$\varphi_l$ normalized by $\varphi_l(r)/r^{l+1}\to1$ and by the outgoing
solution $f_l$ with $f_l(r)=e^{i(kr-l\pi/2)}(1+O(1/r))$: explicitly
$S_l=\overline{W(\varphi_l,f_l)}/W(\varphi_l,f_l)$ and $S_l=e^{2i\delta_l(k)}$
with the phase shift $\delta_l(k)$ defined modulo $\pi$.

(b) $\bigl|\overline{W(\varphi_l,f_l)}\bigr|=\bigl|W(\varphi_l,f_l)\bigr|$, so
$|S_l|=1$, and the total cross section is
$$\sigma=\frac{\pi}{k^2}\sum_{l\ge0}(2l+1)|S_l-1|^2=\frac{4\pi}{k^2}\sum_{l\ge0}(2l+1)\sin^2\delta_l(k),$$
the series converging because $f_k\in L^2(S^2)$ and the expansion in (a) is an
orthogonal expansion.

(c) *Resonance model.* For the single-channel model $S_l(E)=\frac{E-E_r-i\Gamma/2}{E-E_r+i\Gamma/2}$
with $\Gamma>0$ one has $|S_l|=1$ for real $E$ and
$\sin^2\delta_l=\frac{(\Gamma/2)^2}{(E-E_r)^2+(\Gamma/2)^2}$; substituting into
(b) gives the corresponding single-channel cross section. This is a conditional
model calculation, not a theorem that every potential has such a pole.

**(a) Framework data.** Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero, action constant $\hbar>0$, and its stationary elastic beam model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-stationary-beam-and-cross-section-model]] at wave
number $k>0$; adopt the declared central-potential reading of
[[def-nrqm-central-framework-central-potential-model]]: a **declared central
potential** of the pair is a real bounded measurable $V(x)=v(|x|)$ with
$v:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ bounded, and it is **short-range** when it lies in
the compact-support class of the scattering model. Units are those of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]; the wave number $k$ is read in
$\mathrm{m^{-1}}$ and the energy $E=\hbar^{2}k^{2}/(2m)$ in joules.

**(b) Channel vocabulary.** For a declared central short-range potential $V$
and a channel label $(l,m)$ with $l\ge0$ and $-l\le m\le l$, the model
declares the **partial wave** $l$ and reads the angular dependence in the
complete spherical harmonic family $(Y_{lm})$ of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-partial-wave-cross-section-convergence]]; the
labels $l,m$ are indices of that family. The reduced equation below is read in

derivations.claim: Writing $E-E_{r}=x$ and $\Gamma/2=y>0$, the numerator and denominator of $S_{l}(E)=(x-iy)/(x+iy)$ are complex conjugates, so $|S_{l}(E)|=|x-iy|/|x+iy|=1$; this is (a)'s first assertion.

Since $(x-iy)/(x+iy)=\exp(-2i\arctan(y/x))$ for $x\ne0$ by the arctangent addition formula, and $\arctan(y/0^{+})=\pi/2$, the phase shift is $\delta_{l}(E)=-\arctan\frac{\Gamma/2}{E-E_{r}}$ modulo $\pi$; this completes (a).

With $y=\Gamma/2$ and $x=E-E_{r}$, $\sin^{2}\delta_{l}=\sin^{2}\arctan(y/x)=y^{2}/(x^{2}+y^{2})$, which is the display of (b); at $x=0$ the value is $1$, and $\sin^{2}\delta_{l}=1/2$ exactly when $x^{2}=y^{2}$, i.e. at $E=E_{r}\pm\Gamma/2$, so the half-height width in energy is $2\cdot\Gamma/2=\Gamma$.

**What the page establishes, and what it does not.**

- *Model deductions.* The page proves, conditionally on the declared
  short-range model and the cited mathematics, the existence of the wave
  operators, their isometry and intertwining
  ([[pthm-nrqm-scattering-wave-operator-existence-and-free-continuity]]), the
  asymptotic completeness and unitarity of the scattering operator for the
  compact-support and resolvent-tail classes
  ([[pthm-nrqm-scattering-compact-support-asymptotic-completeness]],
  [[pthm-nrqm-scattering-resolvent-tail-asymptotic-completeness]]), the
  stationary outgoing solution with its amplitude and the cross-section
  readings ([[pthm-nrqm-scattering-stationary-wave-amplitude-and-flux]]), the controlled
  Born approximation with its operator-norm condition
  ([[pthm-nrqm-scattering-controlled-born-approximation]]), the phase-shift
  cross-section series, the on-shell operator identification, and the
  conditional resonance-model algebra. Every one of these is a logical
  consequence of the stated postulates, model declarations, hypotheses and
  mathematics; none of them is an observation.
- *No observations.* The page reports no experiment: it contains no apparatus,
  no calibration, no sample, no count, no uncertainty budget and no measured
  cross section. Nothing on the page should be read as a measurement of $V$,
  $\kappa$, a phase shift or a resonance parameter.
- *What a comparison would require.* To compare the model quantities
  $d\sigma/d\Omega$ or $\sigma$ with data one needs a declared target
  preparation (target density and composition), an incident fluence with its
  own uncertainty, a stated scattering geometry, a detector acceptance and
  efficiency model, and a background model, together with a declared
  statistical model for the counts. The equal-channel elastic flux assumptions
  of the beam model ([[def-nrqm-scattering-stationary-beam-and-cross-section-model]]
  clause (d)) must be justified for the particular apparatus; inelastic or
  multichannel processes lie outside the model and would require separate
  channels.
- *Interpretation.* Agreement of a measured count rate with the model reading
  is evidence for the combined model-plus-apparatus assumptions; it is not a
  deduction that the declared model, its potential class or the framework
  describes nature. Disagreement would not by itself falsify the whole
  framework, and a finite dataset can be compatible with a model without
  confirming it.

**Scope of the model declarations.** The potential is prescribed, not derived;
the Coulomb coupling $\kappa$ and the resonance parameters $E_{r},\Gamma$ are
model parameters, not measured constants; and the modified Dollard comparison
of the Coulomb model is a declared construction whose phase convention changes
only asymptotic channel phases
([[def-nrqm-scattering-coulomb-dollard-model]] clauses (c), (d)).

## Remarks

- **Long-range tails.** The short-range classes of
  [[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] clause (b) exclude the
  pure Coulomb tail: the decaying-tail criterion of
  [[pthm-nrqm-scattering-resolvent-tail-asymptotic-completeness]] clause (c)
  requires a positive power $\delta>0$, and the Coulomb quotient
  $(1+|x|)^{1+\delta}|V(x)|$ is unbounded for every $\delta>0$. The Coulomb
  case is treated by the modified Dollard comparison
  ([[def-nrqm-scattering-coulomb-dollard-model]]), for which the ordinary
  short-range comparison is not claimed.

  declared classes and do not require a zero-energy nonresonance hypothesis
  ([[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-resolvent-tail-short-range-completeness]]).
  A different uniformity statement fails at zero energy: for compactly
  supported potentials the scattering defects are not compact uniformly when
  the energy cutoff does not vanish at $0$
  ([[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-compact-scattering-defects]]). The page
  therefore asserts nothing about the stationary problem at $k=0$, and every
  stationary statement of the pair is made for $k>0$.
- **Positive eigenvalues.** The absence of positive eigenvalues is part of
  [[pthm-nrqm-scattering-wave-operator-existence-and-free-continuity]] clause
  (d) for the compact-support class; no statement is made about negative or

  belongs to this page.

  ([[def-nrqm-scattering-single-channel-resonance-model]]) is a declared
  conditional model; the page proves no existence of a resonance for any
  declared potential and makes no analytic-continuation claim for the
  resolvent or the scattering operator.

## Example

**Setup.** Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero, action constant $\hbar>0$, and declare the **spherical square well**
$$V(x):=\begin{cases}-U,&|x|<a,\\ 0,&|x|\ge a,\end{cases}\qquad U>0,\ a>0,$$
read in joules and metres; $V$ is real, bounded and compactly supported, so it
is in the compact-support class. Adopt the central stationary reading at wave
number $k>0$ of
[[def-nrqm-scattering-partial-wave-and-phase-shift-readings]] and the
$s$-wave ($l=0$) channel. Put
$$K:=\frac{\sqrt{2m(E+U)}}{\hbar},\qquad k:=\frac{\sqrt{2mE}}{\hbar},\qquad E>0 .$$
Because the declared potential is constant on each of the two regions and
bounded, the reduced radial function $u_0:=\varphi_0$ of the cited channel
vocabulary (up to a nonzero real normalization) is $C^1$ at $r=a$
with second derivative given by the reduced equation on each side, and the
$s$-wave phase shift is determined by matching: $u_{0}\propto\sin(Kr)$ for
$r<a$ and $u_{0}\propto\sin(kr+\delta_{0})$ for $r>a$.

The phase is read modulo $\pi$. For $z=X+iY\ne0$, $\arg z$ means an angle $\theta$ modulo $2\pi$ with $\cos\theta=X/|z|$ and $\sin\theta=Y/|z|$; hence $\arg z$ modulo $\pi$ determines the phase without dividing by $X$ or $Y$. Big-$O$ terms below are for $k\to0^+$ at a fixed depth and radius; depth comparisons are taken after that low-energy limit.

## Verification

**Given:** the data of the setup and the reduced equation of the $s$-wave of
[[def-nrqm-scattering-partial-wave-and-phase-shift-readings]] clause (b).

[F1] The actual channel supplier defines the regular function itself as the reduced radial solution, with $\varphi_0(r)/r\to1$ at the origin, the exterior outgoing function $e^{ikr}$ and the channel ratio $S_0=\overline{W(u_0,e^{ikr})}/W(u_0,e^{ikr})=e^{2i\delta_0}$. Its channel cross-section is $\sigma_0=4\pi\sin^2\delta_0/k^2$ ([[def-nrqm-scattering-partial-wave-and-phase-shift-readings]] clauses (b),(c), [[pthm-nrqm-scattering-partial-wave-cross-section]] clauses (b),(c)).

[F2] The derivatives of sine and cosine and $\sin^2x+\cos^2x=1$ are [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]] and [[cor-trigonometric-parity-and-pythagorean-identity]]. The finite Taylor remainder estimate with a locally bounded next derivative is [[cor-taylor-remainder-bound]]. The existence of a zero between opposite signs of a continuous real function is [[thm-intermediate-value]]; strict decrease follows from a negative derivative by [[cor-mean-value-theorem]].

[F3] For a radial function $f(x)=u(|x|)/|x|$, polar integration gives $\|f\|_2^2=4\pi\int_0^\infty|u(r)|^2dr$ ([[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]], $n=3$, and $\sigma(S^2)=4\pi$ from [[lem-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-integral-in-angle-coordinates]] clause (b)). The weak domain $W^{2,2}$ requires square-integrable weak derivatives through order two ([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]), and the declared bounded-well energy operator has that domain and acts as $-c\Delta+V$, $c=\hbar^2/(2m)$ ([[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] clause (c)).

1.1 For $r<a$ the reduced equation is $u_0''=-K^2u_0$, so its nonzero real regular solution is $u_0(r)=A\sin(Kr)$, $A\ne0$, with $u_0(0)=0$; the normalization in [F1] corresponds to $A=1/K$. For $r>a$ a nonzero real solution has the form $B\sin(kr+\delta_0)$ with real $B\ne0$. The regular solution and its derivative are absolutely continuous locally through the bounded step potential; integrating the radial equation across $a$ gives no jump of $u_0'$ or $u_0$. Thus $A\sin(Ka)=B\sin(ka+\delta_0)$ and $AK\cos(Ka)=Bk\cos(ka+\delta_0)$. [given, F1, algebra]

2.1 Put $X:=K\cos(Ka)$, $Y:=k\sin(Ka)$ and $z:=X+iY$. Since $k,K>0$ and sine and cosine cannot both vanish, $X^2+Y^2>0$. With $\theta:=ka+\delta_0$, the matching equations give $Bk\cos\theta=AX$, $Bk\sin\theta=AY$, hence $e^{2i\theta}=z/\overline z$ regardless of the real sign of $A/B$. Consequently $S_0(k)=e^{-2ika}\,(K\cos(Ka)+ik\sin(Ka))/(K\cos(Ka)-ik\sin(Ka))$ and $\delta_0=\arg z-ka$ modulo $\pi$, with a nonzero denominator for every positive energy and depth. This is also the actual Wronskian convention of [F1], since outside the well $W(u_0,e^{ikr})=-Bk e^{-i\delta_0}$. Where $\cos(Ka)\ne0$, the equivalent local formula is $\tan(ka+\delta_0)=(k/K)\tan(Ka)$; the complex formula remains valid when either matching value vanishes. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Fix $U>0$ and put $\gamma:=\sqrt{2mU}/\hbar$, so $K=\sqrt{\gamma^2+k^2}$ and $K-\gamma=k^2/(K+\gamma)=O(k^2)$. If $\cos(\gamma a)\ne0$, choose the representative of $\theta$ tending to zero modulo $\pi$. The tangent is smooth near $\gamma a$, so $\tan\theta=(k/K)\tan(Ka)=k\tan(\gamma a)/\gamma+O(k^3)$. By [F2], $\tan\theta=\theta+O(\theta^3)$ near zero; first $\theta=O(k)$ and then $\theta=k\tan(\gamma a)/\gamma+O(k^3)$. Hence $\delta_0=-k a_{\mathrm{eff}}+O(k^3)$ modulo $\pi$, where $a_{\mathrm{eff}}:=a-\tan(\gamma a)/\gamma$, and [F1] gives $\sigma_0\to4\pi a_{\mathrm{eff}}^2$. The expansion uses locally bounded derivatives only where $\cos(\gamma a)\ne0$. [F1, F2, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 At an exact threshold $\gamma a=\alpha_n:=(n+\tfrac12)\pi$, $n\ge0$, write $s_n:=\sin\alpha_n=(-1)^n$. The identity for $K-\gamma$ and [F2] give $K-\gamma=k^2/(2\gamma)+O(k^4)$, $X=K\cos(Ka)=-s_n a k^2/2+O(k^4)$ and $Y=k\sin(Ka)=s_n k+O(k^5)$. Thus $X/Y=-ak/2+O(k^3)$ and the angle of $X+iY$ tends to $\pi/2$ modulo $\pi$. Writing $\theta=\pi/2+\varepsilon$ modulo $\pi$, $\cot\theta=-\varepsilon+O(\varepsilon^3)$ gives $\varepsilon=ak/2+O(k^3)$, so $\delta_0=\pi/2-ak/2+O(k^3)$ modulo $\pi$. Therefore $k^2\sigma_0=4\pi\sin^2\delta_0\to4\pi$; the finite-scattering-length formula of step 3.1 does not apply at this depth. At zero energy the regular reduced solution is proportional to $\sin(\gamma r)$ inside and to the nonzero constant $s_n$ outside, with matching derivative zero at $a$. Its spatial form is proportional to $1/r$ outside and is not square integrable by [F3]; this is the zero-energy s-wave resonance meant here. [F1, F2, F3, step 2.1, algebra]

5.1 In the finite-length branch, as $\gamma a\uparrow\alpha_n$ from below, $\tan(\gamma a)\to+\infty$ and $a_{\mathrm{eff}}\to-\infty$; from above $a_{\mathrm{eff}}\to+\infty$. Thus the iterated low-energy reading $4\pi a_{\mathrm{eff}}^2$ diverges on either approach, while the exact-threshold law is step 4.1. Along nonresonant depth regimes with $\tan(\gamma a)/\gamma\to0$, $a_{\mathrm{eff}}\to a$ and the iterated low-energy reading tends to $4\pi a^2$, four times the geometric area $\pi a^2$. In particular at $\gamma a=n\pi$, $n\ge1$, $a_{\mathrm{eff}}=a$ and $\delta_0=-ka+O(k^3)$; the interior node tends to the boundary. This comparison holds along the stated depth regimes, rather than for every sequence of large depths. [F1, F2, step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra]

5.2 The bound-state interpretation has a separate negative-energy proof. Write $g:=\gamma a$. For $\alpha_n<g<(n+1)\pi$, define $f_g(x):=x\cot x+\sqrt{g^2-x^2}$ on $[\alpha_n,g]$. It is continuous, $f_g(\alpha_n)=\sqrt{g^2-\alpha_n^2}>0$ and $f_g(g)=g\cot g<0$; [F2] gives a root $x_g\in(\alpha_n,g)$. On that open interval $f_g'=\cot x-x\csc^2x-x/\sqrt{g^2-x^2}<0$, so the root is unique. Put $q:=x_g/a$, $\kappa:=\sqrt{g^2-x_g^2}/a>0$ and $u(r):=\sin(qr)$ for $r\le a$, $u(r):=\sin(qa)e^{-\kappa(r-a)}$ for $r\ge a$. Then $q^2+\kappa^2=\gamma^2$ and $q\cot(qa)=-\kappa$, so both $u$ and $u'$ match at $a$. The spatial function $\psi(x):=u(|x|)/|x|$, with value $q$ at zero, is nonzero and square integrable by [F3]; it is smooth near zero, decays exponentially at infinity and is piecewise smooth with matching first derivatives at $a$. Its weak derivatives through order two are square integrable, with no boundary delta term, hence $\psi\in W^{2,2}$. The radial identity $\Delta(u(r)/r)=u''(r)/r$ for $r>0$ gives $H\psi=-c\kappa^2\psi$, $c=\hbar^2/(2m)$, so normalization produces a genuine s-wave bound eigenvector. As $g\downarrow\alpha_n$, $0<\kappa a\le\sqrt{g^2-\alpha_n^2}\to0$, while for $g\le\alpha_n$ there is no matching root in this branch $x>\alpha_n$ with $x\le g$. Thus a new negative-energy s-wave branch appears just above each stated threshold, whose endpoint is the non-square-integrable zero-energy resonance in step 4.1; no assertion about other angular channels or the full bound-state count is needed. [F2, F3, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 For the free consistency case $U=0$, $K=k$ and step 2.1 gives $S_0=e^{-2ika}(\cos ka+i\sin ka)/(\cos ka-i\sin ka)=1$, so $\delta_0=0$ modulo $\pi$ at every positive energy, including zeros of sine or cosine. At any positive-depth energy with $Ka=n\pi$, $n\ge1$, one has $Y=0$ and $X\ne0$, hence $S_0=e^{-2ika}$ and $\delta_0=-ka$ modulo $\pi$: this is exactly the exterior phase for the vanishing radial boundary condition of a hard sphere at that energy. If $\cos(Ka)=0$, the same formula gives $S_0=-e^{-2ika}$ and $\delta_0=\pi/2-ka$ modulo $\pi$. These checks complete the full positive-energy, zero-depth and matching-node cases together with the two low-energy branches above. ## Remarks

- **What is asserted.** The phase shift, both low-energy branches, the locally proved s-wave bound-state threshold and the
  hard-sphere comparison are exact consequences of the declared well and the
  channel vocabulary; no measured phase shift or cross section is reported,
  and no claim is made that the spherical square well describes any material
  target.
- **Idealisation.** The well is an idealised declared potential: it is
  discontinuous at $|x|=a$, and the depth comparisons of steps 4.1 and 5.1

derivations.claim: For $r<a$ the reduced equation with $l=0$ is $u_{0}''=-K^{2}u_{0}$, whose regular solution at the origin is $u_{0}(r)=A\sin(Kr)$ with $u_{0}(0)=0$; for $r>a$ it is $u_{0}''=-k^{2}u_{0}$, whose most general solution with the outgoing reading of the channel vocabulary is $u_{0}(r)=B\sin(kr+\delta_{0})$. Boundedness of the potential makes $u_{0}''$ bounded near $r=a$, so $u_{0}'$ is continuous and $u_{0}$ is $C^{1}$ there, and continuity of $u_{0}$ and $u_{0}'$ at $r=a$ gives $A\sin(Ka)=B\sin(ka+\delta_{0})$ and $AK\cos(Ka)=Bk\cos(ka+\delta_{0})$.

Dividing the two matching equations eliminates $A,B$ and gives $K\cot(Ka)=k\cot(ka+\delta_{0})$, that is $\tan(ka+\delta_{0})=(k/K)\tan(Ka)$; hence $\delta_{0}(k)=\arctan\bigl((k/K)\tan(Ka)\bigr)-ka$ modulo $\pi$. Both $k$ and $K$ are real and positive, so the right side is real; the channel factor $S_{0}=e^{2i\delta_{0}}$ has modulus one by [[pthm-nrqm-scattering-partial-wave-cross-section]] clause (b).

Let $E\to0^{+}$, so $k\to0$ and $K\to K_{0}:=\sqrt{2mU}/\hbar$. Since $(k/K)\tan(Ka)\to0$, the first term is $\arctan\bigl((k/K)\tan(Ka)\bigr)=k\tan(K_{0}a)/K_{0}+O(k^{3})$, hence $\delta_{0}(k)=-k\,a_{\mathrm{eff}}+O(k^{3})$ with $a_{\mathrm{eff}}:=a-\tan(K_{0}a)/K_{0}$, and the s-wave channel reading of [[pthm-nrqm-scattering-partial-wave-cross-section]] clause (b) is $\sigma_{0}=4\pi\sin^{2}\delta_{0}/k^{2}\to4\pi a_{\mathrm{eff}}^{2}$.

The low-energy behaviour separates two depth regimes. If $K_{0}a\to(n+\frac12)\pi$ from below, then $\tan(K_{0}a)\to+\infty$ and $a_{\mathrm{eff}}\to-\infty$, so the low-energy $s$-wave cross-section reading $4\pi a_{\mathrm{eff}}^{2}$ diverges: this is the zero-energy resonance of the well at which a new bound state appears, not a hard-sphere limit. If instead $\tan(K_{0}a)/K_{0}\to0$, then $a_{\mathrm{eff}}\to a$ and $\sigma_{0}\to4\pi a^{2}$, the low-energy $s$-wave reading of a hard sphere of radius $a$, four times its geometric cross section $\pi a^{2}$; at the depths $K_{0}a=n\pi$ of this class one has $\tan(K_{0}a)=0$ exactly, hence $a_{\mathrm{eff}}=a$ and $\delta_{0}(k)=-ka+O(k^{3})$, and the interior regular solution has a node approaching $r=a$, which is the vanishing boundary condition of the hard sphere.

As a consistency check of the matching algebra, set $U=0$; then $K=k$ and the relation $K\cot(Ka)=k\cot(ka+\delta_{0})$ gives $\delta_{0}=0$ modulo $\pi$, which is the correct free case; and at an energy with $\tan(Ka)=0$, i.e. $Ka=n\pi$, the matching gives $k\cot(ka+\delta_{0})=K\cot(Ka)\to\infty$, i.e. $\sin(ka+\delta_{0})=0$, so $\delta_{0}=-ka$ modulo $\pi$: at such an energy the interior solution vanishes at $r=a$ and the exterior phase is that of a hard sphere of radius $a$.

after.quote:
**(a) Framework data.** Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero, action constant $\hbar>0$, and its stationary elastic beam model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-stationary-beam-and-cross-section-model]] at wave
number $k>0$; adopt the declared central-potential reading of
[[def-nrqm-central-framework-central-potential-model]]: a **declared central
potential** of the pair is a real bounded measurable $V(x)=v(|x|)$ with
$v:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ bounded, and it is **short-range** when it lies in
the compact-support class of the scattering model. Units are those of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]; the wave number $k$ is read in
$\mathrm{m^{-1}}$ and the energy $E=\hbar^{2}k^{2}/(2m)$ in joules.

**(b) Channel vocabulary.** For a declared central short-range potential $V$
and a channel label $(l,m)$ with $l\ge0$ and $-l\le m\le l$, the model
declares the **partial wave** $l$ and reads the angular dependence in the
complete spherical harmonic family $(Y_{lm})$ of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-partial-wave-cross-section-convergence]]; the
labels $l,m$ are indices of that family. The reduced equation below is read in
the pair's nondimensional normalization: the reduced potential is
$w:=2mv/\hbar^{2}$ of clause (c) of
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] and the energy is $k^{2}$,
so that the physical parameters $m,\hbar$ do not enter it explicitly. The
model declares the **regular radial solution**
$\varphi_{l}$ of the reduced equation
$$-\varphi_{l}''+\Bigl(w(r)+\frac{l(l+1)}{r^{2}}\Bigr)\varphi_{l}=k^{2}\varphi_{l}, \qquad \varphi_{l}(r)/r^{l+1}\longrightarrow1\quad(r\to0),$$
and the **outgoing radial solution** $f_{l}$ with
$$f_{l}(r)=e^{i(kr-l\pi/2)}\bigl(1+O(r^{-1})\bigr)\qquad(r\to\infty)$$
outside the interaction region; these are the functions constructed by the
cited theorem, and they are not asserted to be elements of the state space.

**(c) Channel factor and phase shift.** The model declares the **channel
factor** and the **phase shift** of the partial wave $l$ to be
$$S_{l}(k):=\frac{\overline{W(\varphi_{l},f_{l})}}{W(\varphi_{l},f_{l})}, \qquad S_{l}(k)=e^{2i\delta_{l}(k)},$$
where $W(\varphi_{l},f_{l})=\varphi_{l}f_{l}'-\varphi_{l}'f_{l}$ is the
Wronskian and $\delta_{l}(k)$ is the **phase shift**, a real number read
modulo $\pi$; the model reads $|S_{l}(k)|=1$ and calls the channel
**elastic**. The declared **channel cross-section reading** is
$$\sigma_{l}(k):=\frac{4\pi}{k^{2}}(2l+1)\sin^{2}\delta_{l}(k),$$
read in $\mathrm{m^{2}}$. The existence of the functions and the identities
$|S_{l}|=1$ and $\sum_{l}(2l+1)\sin^{2}\delta_{l}<\infty$ are proved on this
page and are not presupposed here.

**(d) Status and scope.** Clauses (b)-(c) are declarations of the pair: names
for the objects constructed by the cited mathematics and the reading of the
phase shift modulo $\pi$. The model asserts no identification of the labels
$l,m$ with a measured angular momentum of a material system, no statement
about bound states or their count, and no channel decomposition for
non-central potentials. Every numerical statement about $\delta_{l}$ is a
separate theorem or example of the pair.

Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero and a **declared central short-range potential** $V(x)=v(|x|)$ in the
sense of [[def-nrqm-scattering-partial-wave-and-phase-shift-readings]]
clause (a): $v$ is real, bounded and $V$ is supported in a ball $B_{R}$. Adopt
the stationary elastic beam model at wave number $k>0$ and direction
$d\in S^{2}$, with amplitude $f_{k}$ as in
[[pthm-nrqm-scattering-stationary-wave-amplitude-and-flux]], and the
channel vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-scattering-partial-wave-and-phase-shift-readings]] clauses (b),
(c). Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) $f_{k}$ depends only on $\cos\theta=\Omega\cdot d$, and its **Legendre
expansion**
$$f_{k}(\theta)=\frac{1}{2ik}\sum_{l\ge0}(2l+1)\bigl(S_{l}(k)-1\bigr)P_{l}(\cos\theta)$$
converges in $L^{2}(S^{2})$ and absolutely, so the model's cross-section
reading is
$$\frac{d\sigma}{d\Omega}(\theta)=|f_{k}(\theta)|^{2};$$

(b) the channel factors are unit modulus, $|S_{l}(k)|=1$, the phase shifts
$\delta_{l}(k)$ are real modulo $\pi$, and the **total cross section** of the
beam model is
$$\sigma=\frac{\pi}{k^{2}}\sum_{l\ge0}(2l+1)|S_{l}(k)-1|^{2} =\frac{4\pi}{k^{2}}\sum_{l\ge0}(2l+1)\sin^{2}\delta_{l}(k)\qquad\text{in }\mathrm{m^{2}},$$
the series converging, with the channel readings of
[[def-nrqm-scattering-partial-wave-and-phase-shift-readings]] clause (c) as
its summands;

(c) the objects $\varphi_{l}$, $f_{l}$, $S_{l}$ and $\delta_{l}$ of the
channel vocabulary are exactly the regular and outgoing radial solutions, the
Wronskian ratio and the phase shift constructed by the cited mathematics for
the reduced radial potential $w=(2m/\hbar^2)v$ at the model's wave number $k$; the phase shifts
are not asserted to have a definite sign and no low-energy limit is asserted
beyond the convergence of the series.

The statement is conditional on the declared central model, the beam model
and the cited mathematics; it asserts no measured angular distribution and no
identification of $l$ with a measured angular momentum.

The functions $\sin$ and $\cos$ are differentiable on $\mathbb R$, with
$$(\sin x)'=\cos x,\qquad(\cos x)'=-\sin x.$$
Also $\sin0=0$ and $\cos0=1$.

For every real $x$,
$$\sin(-x)=-\sin x,\qquad\cos(-x)=\cos x,\qquad\sin^2x+\cos^2x=1.$$
Consequently $|\sin x|\le1$ and $|\cos x|\le1$.

Let $n\in\mathbb N$, and suppose $f$ has derivatives through order $n+1$ on the closed interval between $a$ and $x$, with the usual endpoint continuity. If $|f^{(n+1)}(t)|\le M$ throughout that interval, then
$$|R_{n,a}f(x)|\le \frac{M}{\iota((n+1)!)}|x-a|^{n+1}.$$

Let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$ with $a \le b$, let $f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be
continuous on the closed bounded interval $[a,b]$ ([[def-interval]],
[[def-continuity-real]]), and let $y \in \mathbb{R}$ satisfy

$$f(a) \le y \le f(b) \qquad \text{or} \qquad f(b) \le y \le f(a) .$$

Then there is $c \in [a,b]$ with $f(c) = y$.

**The construction is canonical, so no choice principle is used.** The bisection
below tests the left half first and takes the right half only when the left one
has been ruled out, so the passage from one interval to the next is a *function*
of that interval, and [[thm-recursion]] applies with nothing selected. This is
the same discipline the library uses wherever a sequence is built one term at a
time.

**Completeness of $\mathbb{R}$ is what does the work.** The bisection produces a
nested sequence of closed bounded intervals whose lengths tend to $0$, and it is
[[thm-nested-interval-property]] — hence the least-upper-bound property — that
supplies the point. Over an ordered field that is not complete the theorem
fails; the witness for that, stated for an arbitrary ordered field and worked
over $\mathbb{Q}$, is
[[cex-evt-and-ivt-fail-over-a-non-complete-field]], which states its own
$\varepsilon$-$\delta$ continuity inline and is not an instance of this page's
definition.

Let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$ with $a < b$ and let $f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be
continuous on $[a,b]$ ([[def-continuity-real]], [[def-interval]]) and
differentiable at every point of $(a,b)$ as a function on $[a,b]$
([[def-derivative]]). Then there is $c \in (a,b)$ with

$$f(b) - f(a) \;=\; f'(c)\,(b - a) .$$

Equivalently, since $b - a \ne 0$, there is $c \in (a,b)$ at which
$f'(c) = \bigl(f(b)-f(a)\bigr)/(b-a)$: the derivative somewhere inside equals
the average rate of change across the whole interval.

**Continuity on the closed interval cannot be dropped.** Differentiability at
every point of $(a,b)$ alone does not suffice: a function on $[0,1]$,
differentiable at every point of $(0,1)$ with derivative constantly $1$, for
which no $c$ works, is exhibited later on this page as a false statement, and
the companion page works the same witness out in full.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $n \ge 1$,
let $S^{n-1} \subseteq \mathbb R^n$ be the unit sphere, and let $\sigma$ be the
set function of [[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]]. Then $\sigma$
is a finite Borel measure on $S^{n-1}$, and for every Borel measurable
$f : \mathbb R^n \to [0,\infty]$,
$$\int_{\mathbb R^n} f(x)\,d\lambda_n(x) = \int_0^\infty \int_{S^{n-1}} f(r\omega) r^{n-1}\,d\sigma(\omega)\,dr.$$
Moreover, $\sigma$ is the unique Borel measure on $S^{n-1}$ with this
property.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$S^2:=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:|x|=1\}$ and let $\sigma$ be the polar surface measure on $S^2$ of
[[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]], a finite Borel measure ([[def-measure]],
[[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). Let

$$\Phi:(0,\pi)\times(0,2\pi)\to S^2,\qquad \Phi(\theta,\varphi):=(\sin\theta\cos\varphi,\ \sin\theta\sin\varphi,\ \cos\theta),$$

and let $H:=\{(x,y,0)\in\mathbb R^3:x\ge0\}$ denote the closed half-plane, a Lebesgue-null Borel set
([[thm-affine-hyperplanes-and-proper-subspaces-of-rn-are-lebesgue-null]]). Then:

(a) for every Borel function $F:S^2\to[0,+\infty]$,
$$\int_{S^2}F\,d\sigma=\int_{(0,\pi)\times(0,2\pi)}F\bigl(\Phi(\theta,\varphi)\bigr)\,\sin\theta\ d(\theta,\varphi),$$
the right-hand integral being the Lebesgue integral over the open rectangle;

(b) $\sigma(S^2)=4\pi$;

(c) the identity of (a) holds with $F\in L^1(S^2,\sigma;\mathbb C)$ in the sense that $F\circ\Phi$ is Lebesgue
integrable on the rectangle against $\sin\theta\,d(\theta,\varphi)$ and the two integrals agree (real and
imaginary parts, positive and negative parts).

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, $k\in\mathbb N_0$, $1\le p\le\infty$, and
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. Write
$$\mathcal A_k=\{\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^n:|\alpha|\le k\}.$$
This is a finite nonempty set: every coordinate of such an $\alpha$ lies in
$\{0,\ldots,k\}$, and it contains the zero multi-index.

The real and complex $L^p$ classes use the conventions in
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]] and
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]. Their quotient
norm values are supplied by
[[thm-the-l-p-norm-descends-to-the-quotient-and-makes-l-p-a-normed-space]]
for real scalars and
[[thm-complex-holder-minkowski-and-the-quotient-norm]] for complex scalars.

Define $W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ to be the set of classes
$u\in L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ such that, for every $\alpha\in\mathcal A_k$,
there is an $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ class with a locally integrable
representative $v_\alpha$ satisfying
$$\int_\Omega u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,dx =(-1)^{|\alpha|}\int_\Omega v_\alpha\varphi\,dx \qquad\text{for every }\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega).$$
Here the weak derivative is the one in
[[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]. Under
[[def-countable-choice]], local integrability of $L^p$ representatives and
invariance under null-set changes follow from
[[lem-weak-derivative-is-independent-of-lp-representatives]], while
[[lem-weak-derivatives-are-unique-almost-everywhere]] gives uniqueness of each
locally integrable derivative class. Thus this condition is a condition on the
$L^p$ class $u$, and each resulting derivative determines one $L^p$ class,
denoted $D^\alpha u$. The test pairing is bilinear, without conjugation.

For the zero multi-index, set $D^0u=u$. Since $\mathcal A_0=\{0\}$,
$$W^{0,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)=L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K).$$
The Sobolev norm expression is
$$\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}= \begin{cases} \left(\displaystyle\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_k} \|D^\alpha u\|_{L^p(\Omega)}^p\right)^{1/p},&1\le p<\infty,\\[1ex] \displaystyle\max_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_k} \|D^\alpha u\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)},&p=\infty. \end{cases}$$
The formula is finite because each derivative class belongs to $L^p$ and
$\mathcal A_k$ is finite; at $k=0$ it reduces to the $L^p$ norm expression.
The finite maximum is defined because $\mathcal A_k$ is nonempty. The norm
axioms for this expression are a separate assertion from this definition.

For open $U\subseteq\Omega$ with $\overline U$ compact and contained in
$\Omega$, the notation $W^{k,p}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ means that
the restriction of the class belongs to $W^{k,p}(U;\mathbb K)$ for every such
$U$.

If $\Omega=\varnothing$, the $L^p$ space and every $W^{k,p}$ space contain
only the zero class, and the displayed norm expression is zero.

**(a) Framework data.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the
observable and probability postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4,
the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5, the identical-particle
and spin postulate P6, and the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]). Fix a mass parameter
$m>0$ and a spin label $s=0$, so that the framework's one-particle model
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] reads its state space as
$H_{0}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ with the pairing linear in the first
argument, its componentwise position family $Q_{1},Q_{2},Q_{3}$, its
componentwise momentum family $P_{1},P_{2},P_{3}$ and the action constant
$\hbar>0$; the spin-zero internal factor carries the trivial representation of
P6. Units are those of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]: position
is read in metres, momentum in $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$, energy and potential
energy in joules, and $\hbar$ in $\mathrm{J\,s}$. Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice as the choice hypotheses of the cited
mathematical suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(b) The declared scattering model and its potential classes.** As an
additional model assumption of the pair, adopt the **short-range scattering
model**. Its declared state space is $H_{0}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ of
clause (a), with the position and momentum families of that clause. A
**declared short-range potential** of the model is a real-valued measurable
function $V:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R$ satisfying either

1. *(compact-support class)* $V$ is bounded, $\|V\|_{\infty}<\infty$, and
   $V=0$ almost everywhere outside some ball
   $B_{\mathrm{supp}}:=\{x:|x|\le R_{\mathrm{supp}}\}$ with
   $R_{\mathrm{supp}}<\infty$; or
2. *(resolvent-tail class)* $V=V_{2}+V_{\mathrm b}$ with real
   $V_{2}\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3})$ and real bounded $V_{\mathrm b}$, and, with
   the reduced potential $W:=2mV/\hbar^{2}:=W_{2}+W_{\mathrm b}$ and the
   nondimensional free operator $A_{0}:=-\Delta_{w}$ of clause (c) (so that
   $H^{\mathrm{free}}=(\hbar^{2}/2m)A_{0}$), the function
$$h(r):=\bigl\|M_{W}(A_{0}-i)^{-1}\mathbf 1_{\{|x|\ge r\}}\bigr\|, \qquad r\ge0,$$
   is finite for every $r$ and belongs to $L^{1}([0,\infty))$.

The function $V$ is read as a potential energy in joules; the model asserts no
derivation of $V$ from P5 or from any force law, and an assignment of a
concrete target to $V$ is a tested identification in the sense of clause (iii)
of P7 carrying the corresponding uncertainty. The pure Coulomb potential
$V(x)=-\kappa/|x|$, $\kappa>0$, is **not** in either class: it is a declared
long-range model with its own definition and comparison construction
on this page.

**(c) Assigned energy observables.** Let $\mathcal F_{2}$ be the unitary
Plancherel transform of
[[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (b), $c:=2\pi^{2}\hbar^{2}/m$, and let
$$H^{\mathrm{free}}:=\mathcal F_{2}^{*}M_{c|\xi|^{2}}\mathcal F_{2},\qquad D(H^{\mathrm{free}}):=\bigl\{f\in H_{0}:|\xi|^{2}\mathcal F_{2}f\in H_{0}\bigr\}$$
be the free operator of that clause with $d=3$ and $b=0$; by
[[lem-nrqm-central-free-operator-differential-identification]] its domain is
the Sobolev space $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$
([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]) and
$H^{\mathrm{free}}f=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta_{w}f$ with $\Delta_{w}$ the
weak Laplacian ([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]).
Write $A_{0}:=-\Delta_{w}$ for this **nondimensional free operator**, so that
$H^{\mathrm{free}}=(\hbar^{2}/2m)A_{0}$ on the common domain, and
$W:=2mV/\hbar^{2}$ for the **reduced potential** of a declared potential $V$.
With $M_V$ the maximal multiplication operator, $D(M_V)=\{f\in L^2:Vf\in L^2\}$ (bounded and everywhere defined in the compact-support class), the **assigned energy observables** of the model with declared
potential $V$ are the free operator $H^{\mathrm{free}}$ and the interacting
operator
$$H:=H^{\mathrm{free}}+M_{V},\qquad D(H):=D(H^{\mathrm{free}}).$$
The declared energy unit is the joule. For the compact-support class,
clause (c) of the cited theorem makes $H$ self-adjoint on $D(H)$ and bounded
below by $-\|V\|_{\infty}$; for the resolvent-tail class, self-adjointness of
$H$ on the same domain is proved on this page and is not presupposed here. The
model adopts $(H^{\mathrm{free}},\mathrm J)$ and $(H,\mathrm J)$ as assigned
sharp observables in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a), and
reads their flows by [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]
with $U_{\mathrm{free}}(t)=e^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}$ and
$U(t)=e^{-itH/\hbar}$.

**(d) Short-range scattering vocabulary.** For a declared short-range
potential $V$ the model declares the **free asymptotic comparison** to be the
pair of strong limits
$$\Omega_{\pm}:=\operatorname*{s-lim}_{t\to\pm\infty}e^{itH/\hbar}e^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar},$$
which are declared **wave operators** of the model when both limits exist, and
declares the **scattering operator** $S:=\Omega_{+}^{*}\Omega_{-}$ when both
exist and $\Omega_{\pm}$ are isometries. The model says that the pair is
**asymptotically complete** for this $V$ when the two ranges agree with the
subspace
$$H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H):=\{\psi\in H_{0}:\mu^{H}_{\psi}\ll\lambda\},$$
where $\mu^{H}_{\psi}(B):=\langle E_{H}(B)\psi,\psi\rangle$ is the scalar

before.claim: For $r<a$ the reduced equation with $l=0$ is $u_{0}''=-K^{2}u_{0}$, whose regular solution at the origin is $u_{0}(r)=A\sin(Kr)$ with $u_{0}(0)=0$; for $r>a$ it is $u_{0}''=-k^{2}u_{0}$, whose most general solution with the outgoing reading of the channel vocabulary is $u_{0}(r)=B\sin(kr+\delta_{0})$. Boundedness of the potential makes $u_{0}''$ bounded near $r=a$, so $u_{0}'$ is continuous and $u_{0}$ is $C^{1}$ there, and continuity of $u_{0}$ and $u_{0}'$ at $r=a$ gives $A\sin(Ka)=B\sin(ka+\delta_{0})$ and $AK\cos(Ka)=Bk\cos(ka+\delta_{0})$.
